faq: Can the review request go to Google or Trustpilot?
Yes. We can link to the review site you choose. We ask every customer the same way and never filter to send only happy buyers to public reviews, because review platforms forbid that.
How do you time the review message?
We use the delivery date where your store records it, or a fixed delay after shipping. Asking before the parcel arrives leads to poor reviews, so timing is something we check carefully.
Will it clash with my shipping emails from the store?
We review both so they do not repeat each other. If your store already sends good shipping messages, we leave them in place and add our messages around them.
How does the reorder reminder know when to send?
We use how long your product usually lasts, which you tell us, such as 30 days for a supplement. You can change the timing per product later without our help.

desc:
Post-purchase email and SMS flows keep the conversation going after the order. Ecom Swift LLC builds thank-you, usage, review and reorder messages in your own email tool, using the order details so each one reads as personal.

## What are post-purchase flows?

Post-purchase flows are automated messages that send after a customer buys. They can include a thank-you with order details, tips for using or caring for the product, a review request after delivery, a related product suggestion and a reminder to reorder.

The aim is a better customer experience first. A shopper who feels looked after is more likely to leave an honest review, contact you with questions and return later.

## Why the time after the sale matters

Winning a first order costs effort and often ad spend. The weeks after delivery are the cheapest moment to build a relationship, because the customer already knows you and is waiting for the parcel. Silence at that point wastes the chance.

The order confirmation from the store is only a receipt. It does not teach, ask or invite. A planned series fills that gap. A how-to message cuts down on support questions. A review request timed after delivery catches the customer when the product is in hand. A reorder reminder appears near the time a consumable might run out. Results vary with product type and customer base, but each message has a clear job.

## What a strong post-purchase journey includes

- A thank-you email that repeats the order and sets expectations.
- A message on how to use or care for the product, with short steps.
- A review request timed after expected delivery, not after the order.
- A route for unhappy customers to reach support before a public review.
- A cross-sell based on what was bought, not a random list.
- A reorder reminder for products that get used up.
- A different path for first-time buyers and repeat customers.
- Shipping update messages styled to match your brand.
- An optional referral or loyalty invitation.
- SMS steps only for customers who opted in to texts.

## How we build it

We map the journey for your products: what the customer needs to know and when. Then we write and design each message in your own tool, connect it to order events and use the order data for names, items and dates.

The Basic package builds a thank-you and a review request. Standard adds how-to content, cross-sell by product bought, a reorder reminder and a separate path for first-time buyers. Premium builds a fuller journey with SMS, shipping update styling, a support route for unhappy replies, a loyalty or referral invitation, written notes and a handover call. Add-ons include an extra product path, a referral email and a replenishment text. We test with a real order, and check that the flow does not repeat messages your store already sends.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Time the review request after delivery.
- Include a direct way to contact support.
- Match the message to the product bought.
- Keep thank-you messages short and warm.
- Review the flow whenever your shipping partner or products change.

**Avoid:**
- Pushing a sale before the customer has the product.
- Asking only happy customers for reviews or filtering reviews unfairly.
- Sending messages that repeat the store's own order emails.
- Offering discounts so heavy that they teach customers to wait.
- Texting buyers who never agreed to receive texts.

## Who it suits

A store with products that run out, such as skincare or food, can use reorder timing well. A brand that sells items needing instructions can cut confusion with a care message. A seller with few reviews can build a steady, fair review request.

## What we need from you

Share your store link, email tool, brand assets, your best-selling products and how long delivery usually takes. Tell us where you want reviews to go. We never need passwords. Access is given as a collaborator, staff or team user where the platform supports it, and you remain the account owner.
